assumptions.condition: The integer composition matrix \(M\) is fixed and known before replicate wells are observed.
Each observed well is the coordinatewise raw-count sum \(B_{ji}=\sum_{r=1}^{K}\sum_{c=1}^{M_{jr}}V_{jirc}\).
Within each pooled well, the cellular count vectors \(V_{jirc}\) are mutually independent.
For every type \(r\), each \(V_{jirc}\) has law \(P_r\) across composition rows and replicates.
The pooled count vectors \(B_{ji}\) are independent across distinct replicate wells.

novel.justification: Any assay measuring at least three coordinates admits a prespecified exposure coordinate and two distinct response coordinates; this domain restriction belongs only to the causal-certificate layer and leaves unrestricted law recovery unchanged.

assumptions.condition: For each type \(r\), the exogenous variables in the structural representation associated with \(d_r\) are jointly independent.

For every type \(r\), every root \(s\) in \(d_r\) has law \(\operatorname{Pois}(\alpha_{rs})\) with \(\alpha_{rs}>0\), while every non-root \(s\) has conditional kernel \(\operatorname{Pois}(\lambda_{rs,\theta})\) with \(\lambda_{rs,\theta}(v)=\alpha_{rs}+\sum_{k\in\operatorname{pa}_{d_r}(s)}b_{rsk}v_k^{q_{sk}}\) and strictly positive root and declared-edge coefficients.

novel.justification: This paper maintains a stricter Poisson-root positive-polynomial Poisson-DAG subclass as a transparent synthetic and prospective-design benchmark. Source-node Poissonity is imposed here; the broader CPCM framework permits arbitrary source-node laws.

assumptions.condition: Every directed parent--child pair and every admissible nondescendant conditioning set satisfy pairwise identifiability in the sense of Definition 10 of Bodik--Chavez-Demoulin.

Each \(\Theta_{\boldsymbol d}\) and \(\Theta^{\mathrm{in}}_{\boldsymbol d}\) is a prespecified compact rational rectangle, with \(\Theta^{\mathrm{in}}_{\boldsymbol d}\subset\operatorname{int}(\Theta_{\boldsymbol d})\), and with strictly positive root and declared-edge coefficient lower endpoints.

novel.justification: A finite box is a prospective design input that can be calibrated from independent pilot assays; positive lower endpoints describe modules screened to exclude silent roots and vanishing candidate edges. The numerical box used below is only synthetic and is not asserted to be biologically calibrated.

assumptions.condition: The exponent array \(q\) is fixed before observing wells and has positive integer entries for every possible ordered edge.

novel.justification: Fixed low-order exponents encode a prespecified nonlinear benchmark and make finite validation possible. They can be chosen from external mechanistic restrictions, but the three-node exponent pattern below is explicitly synthetic.

assumptions.condition: The allocation satisfies \(\rho\in\Delta_J^{\mathbb Q}\) with \(\rho_j>0\) for every row, and for each split \(S\in\{A,B\}\), \(n_{Sj}/N_S\to\rho_j\) for every composition row \(j\).
The finite-grid weight \(W\) is fixed and positive definite.

When \(p\geq3\) and the ordered embedding \(\iota\) is fixed, every reported scalar component \(\tau_{i_Y,r}\) and \(\tau_{i_Z,r}\) has strictly positive asymptotic variance at \(\boldsymbol D_0,\theta_0\).

definitions.construction: For \(p\geq3\), fix the ordered injection \(\iota:\{X,Y,Z\}\hookrightarrow\{1,\ldots,p\}\) and write \(i_A=\iota(A)\) for \(A\in\{X,Y,Z\}\). Set \(\kappa_{\mathcal T}=\min_{\boldsymbol d\in\mathfrak G}\inf_{\vartheta\in\Theta_{\boldsymbol d}}\sigma_{\min}(J_{\boldsymbol d,\mathcal T}(\vartheta))\). For \(r_{\mathrm{id}}>0\), let \(\Lambda_{\mathcal T}(r_{\mathrm{id}})\) be the minimum squared \(W\)-distance between \(m_{\boldsymbol d,\mathcal T}(\vartheta)\) and \(m_{\boldsymbol d,\mathcal T}(\vartheta')\) over \(\boldsymbol d\in\mathfrak G\), \(\vartheta,\vartheta'\in\Theta_{\boldsymbol d}\), and \(\lVert\vartheta-\vartheta'\rVert_2\geq r_{\mathrm{id}}\), with value \(+\infty\) when this feasible pair set is empty. The displayed loop bounds and the fixed recurrence orders therefore give this literal finite ceiling on every counted operation, including unsuccessful precision passes; the bound is deliberately coarse and makes no polynomial-time claim.

definitions.construction: For \(p\geq3\) and fixed \(\iota\), enumerate the finite admissible input class; propagate directed-rounding Taylor models and recursive Poisson tails through wrong-graph exclusion, local chart injectivity, remote within-graph separation, Jacobian nonsingularity, covariance inversion, and designated-contrast precision; retain the nondominated proof objects.

definitions.name: \((\Xi_0,\mathfrak F_0,\theta_1^\star,\theta_2^\star)\)
definitions.construction: Set \(K=2\), \(p=3\), \(J=2\), fix \(\iota(X)=i_X=1\), \(\iota(Y)=i_Y=2\), and \(\iota(Z)=i_Z=3\), and set \(M_0=\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&2\end{pmatrix}\), \(\mathcal T_0=\{4/5,9/10,97/100\}^3\), \(\mathfrak G=\mathfrak D_3^2\), and \(\preceq_{\mathfrak G}\) to lexicographic order of the two row-major binary adjacency codes. For every \(\boldsymbol d=(d_1,d_2)\), put \(d_{\boldsymbol d}=6+|E(d_1)|+|E(d_2)|\), \(\Theta_{\boldsymbol d}=[1/2,3]^{d_{\boldsymbol d}}\), and \(\Theta^{\mathrm{in}}_{\boldsymbol d}=[3/4,5/2]^{d_{\boldsymbol d}}\), with coordinates ordered by type, then roots by node, then edges by child-parent lexicographic order. Set \(q_{31}=1\) and \(q_{sk}=2\) for every other \(s\neq k\), \(W=I_{54}\), \(\mathcal R_0=\{(1/2,1/2)\}\), \(\rho=(1/2,1/2)\), \(r_{\mathrm{id}}=1/32\), \(R=(12,28,80)\), \(s_{\mathrm{tail}}=10\), \(a_{\mathrm{TM}}=8\), \(b_{\max}=20\), \(c_{\max}=8\), \(\pi_{\mathrm{ar}}=(128,64,512,\mathtt{out})\), \(\alpha=1/20\), \(w_{\max}=1\), and \(N_{\max}=200000\); these values define the complete rational input \(\Xi_0\). Let \(D^\star=\{1\to2,1\to3,2\to3\}\), \(\boldsymbol D_0=(D^\star,D^\star)\), and let the two witness parameters have \(\mu_1=1\), \(\mu_2=2\), and every other root or present-edge coefficient equal to \(1\), giving \(V_1\sim\operatorname{Pois}(\mu_r)\), \(V_2\mid V_1=x\sim\operatorname{Pois}(1+x^2)\), and \(V_3\mid V_1=x,V_2=y\sim\operatorname{Pois}(1+x+y^2)\). The sole refinement \(\mathfrak F_0\), used only if \(\mathfrak C(\Xi_0)\) is \(\mathtt{UNDECIDED}\), replaces \(\mathcal T_0\) by \(\mathcal T_1=\mathcal T_0\cup\{3/4,17/20,19/20\}^3\), \(W\) by \(I_{108}\), \(R\) by \((16,36,96)\), \(s_{\mathrm{tail}}\) by \(12\), \(a_{\mathrm{TM}}\) by \(10\), \(b_{\max}\) by \(24\), \(c_{\max}\) by \(10\), and \(\pi_{\mathrm{ar}}\) by \((192,64,768,\mathtt{out})\), leaving every other entry fixed; the result is \(\Xi_1\), and no second refinement is admissible. The coefficient and exponent boxes are a synthetic prospective-design benchmark, not an assay-calibrated biological model.

definitions.name: \(\mathfrak X_{\mathrm{adm}}\)
definitions.construction: Fix \(K,p,\iota,\mathfrak G,(\Theta_{\boldsymbol d},\Theta^{\mathrm{in}}_{\boldsymbol d}),q,W,\pi_{\mathrm{ar}},\alpha,w_{\max}\), finite \(\mathcal Z_{\mathrm{cand}}\), \(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{adm}}\subset\Delta_J^{\mathbb Q}=\{r\in\mathbb Q_+^J:\sum_{j=1}^{J}r_j=1\}\), and \(\mathcal N_{\mathrm{adm}}\), and caps \(\mathfrak b\). Let \(\mathfrak X_{\mathrm{adm}}\) contain exactly inputs with \(1\leq J\leq J_{\max}\), \(M\in\{0,\ldots,m_{\max}\}^{J\times K}\), \(\mathcal T\subseteq\mathcal Z_{\mathrm{cand}}\) and \(1\leq|\mathcal T|\leq L_{\max}\), \(\rho\in\mathcal R_{\mathrm{adm}}\), \(1\leq R_s\leq R_{\max}\), \(1\leq s_{\mathrm{tail}}\leq s_{\max}\), \(0\leq a_{\mathrm{TM}}\leq a_{\max}\), \(0\leq b_{\max}\leq b_{\max}^{\mathrm{adm}}\), \(0\leq c_{\max}\leq c_{\max}^{\mathrm{adm}}\), \(N_{\max}\in\mathcal N_{\mathrm{adm}}\), and \(\mathfrak B(\Xi)\leq B_{\max}\). All quantities held fixed have finite representations, so the displayed choices form a finite class.

definitions.name: \(\mathfrak P_{\mathrm{adm}}\)
definitions.construction: Let \(\mathfrak P_{\mathrm{adm}}\) be the certified members of \(\mathfrak X_{\mathrm{adm}}\) not weakly dominated with one strict inequality in \((\underline\Gamma_{\mathcal T},\underline\kappa_{\mathcal T},\underline\Lambda_{\mathcal T},\underline\mu_{\mathcal T},-N_{\mathrm{req}},-w_{\mathrm{cert}},-\mathfrak B(\Xi))\).

statements.statement: If \(\operatorname{rank}(M)<K\), every choice in \(\mathfrak A(M,a,\Lambda,u,\epsilon)\) produces two distinct labeled collections of full-support component laws whose row-wise pooled laws are identical.
statements.justification: This supplies a nonboundary necessity witness for the exact rank frontier.
statements.gap: Shih--Hero provides the high-level additive transform-inversion precedent but does not state this positive nullspace alias for arbitrary rank-deficient integer compositions.
statements.consumer: It shows that replication at unchanged composition rows cannot repair a rank-deficient prospective design.

statements.statement: On \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{pool}}\), the pooling map \(\mathscr A_M\) is injective for every labeled \(K\)-tuple \((P_1,\ldots,P_K)\in\mathcal P(\mathbb N_0^p)^K\) if and only if \(\operatorname{rank}(M)=K\). Under full column rank, \((G_1(z),\ldots,G_K(z))^{\mathsf T}=\mathscr R_M(H)(z)\) for every \(z\in(0,1]^p\), and PGF coefficient uniqueness recovers every \(P_r\).
statements.justification: The theorem gives the exact acquisition boundary before causal restrictions or finite-grid estimation are imposed.
statements.gap: Shih--Hero supplies the source-verified high-level idea of transform inversion for independent additive link delays; this theorem credits that idea, derives the displayed count-PGF recovery map, and adds the unrestricted multivariate count-law if-and-only-if frontier with a positive converse family.
statements.consumer: A prospective bulk-mixture study can determine whether its chosen composition rows identify labeled type laws before collecting replicates.

statements.statement: Every member of \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{poly}}(\mathfrak G,\Theta,q)\) has full support on \(\mathbb N_0^p\), is causally sufficient, and is pairwise identifiable in the sense of Bodik--Chavez-Demoulin; hence it belongs to \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{CPCM}}\).
statements.justification: The proposition proves that the nonlinear certificate family lies inside the direct-law identifiable CPCM class.
statements.gap: Bodik--Chavez-Demoulin defines pairwise identifiability and recovers a CPCM DAG from its direct law but does not verify those conditions for this paper's stricter Poisson-root positive-polynomial benchmark family.
statements.consumer: It validates the causal model class searched by the reusable certificate.

statements.statement: Set \(p=3\) and fix the ordered embedding \(\iota(X)=i_X=1\), \(\iota(Y)=i_Y=2\), and \(\iota(Z)=i_Z=3\). For each type \(r\) in the fixed synthetic protocol, the truncated-factorization contrasts satisfy \(\tau_{i_Y,r}=3\) and \(\tau_{i_Z,r}=25\).
statements.justification: This checks the designated-coordinate intervention arithmetic in the synthetic three-node application.
statements.gap: The calculation is an application check and is not presented as a theorem-level novelty claim.
statements.consumer: It supplies auditable contrast targets for the finite-input certificate without treating the synthetic box as biological calibration.

statements.statement: Assume \(p\geq3\) and fix the ordered injection \(\iota:\{X,Y,Z\}\hookrightarrow\{1,\ldots,p\}\). If \(\operatorname{rank}(M)=K\) and every recovered component law belongs to \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{CPCM}}\), then the pooled-law tuple identifies each labeled type graph \(D_r\). If the recovered law belongs to \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{poly}}(\mathfrak G,\Theta,q)\), it also identifies the \(\iota\)-indexed contrast vector \(\boldsymbol\tau=((\tau_{i_Y,r},\tau_{i_Z,r}))_{r=1}^{K}\) through the displayed truncated factorization at \(V_{i_X}\).
statements.justification: This transfers the acquisition certificate to causal structure and supported intervention quantities.
statements.gap: Bodik--Chavez-Demoulin identifies CPCM graphs from direct laws, Gao--Cai--Hara identifies PT-SEM DAGs and thinning parameters from direct count vectors, and Luo--Sun--Zhang Section 4.2 studies functional consistency under linear aggregation and gives affine ANM/PNL consequences; Section 4.3 concerns conditional-independence consistency. Known labeled multi-composition pools remain outside its target, and none of these results recovers labeled causal laws through several independent known-composition mixtures.
statements.consumer: It defines what a successful known-composition prospective bulk assay identifies at the cellular causal level.

statements.statement: If \(\operatorname{rank}(M)=K\) and \(\delta<\beta\), then \(\sup_{z\in\mathcal Z_\eta}\lVert M^{+}\log\widetilde H(z)-\log G(z)\rVert_2\leq E_M\), \(\sup_{z\in\mathcal Z_\eta}\lVert\mathscr R_M(\widetilde H)(z)-G(z)\rVert_2\leq e^{E_M}E_M\), and \(\sup_{z\in\mathcal Z_\eta}\max_r|\mathscr R_M(\widetilde H)_r(z)/G_r(z)-1|\leq e^{E_M}-1\).
statements.justification: The result separates qualitative rank from operational amplification through both \(\lVert M^{+}\rVert_2\) and pooled-PGF attenuation.
statements.gap: Shih--Hero provides the high-level independent-additive transform-inversion precedent but does not supply this multivariate lower-envelope perturbation bound for designed count pools.
statements.consumer: It screens compositions and grid locations before running the more expensive validated certificate.

statements.statement: For any fixed nonempty finite \(\mathfrak G\), nonempty compact boxes, exponent array, and nonempty open \(\mathcal O\subset(0,1)^p\), there are a finite rational \(\mathcal T\subset\mathcal O\), a rational \(r_{\mathrm{id}}>0\), and a valid finite rational chart-projection cover \(\mathscr C\) such that \(\Gamma_{\mathcal T}>0\), \(\kappa_{\mathcal T}>0\), \(\Lambda_{\mathcal T}(r_{\mathrm{id}})>0\), and \(\mu_{\mathcal T}(r_{\mathrm{id}};\mathscr C)>0\). Here \(\Gamma_{\mathcal T}=+\infty\) when \(|\mathfrak G|=1\), and \(\Lambda_{\mathcal T}=+\infty\) when its remote pair set is empty. Consequently each within-graph moment map is globally injective; this uses local chart strong monotonicity and remote separation, not the Jacobian margin alone.
statements.justification: This establishes existence of a finite transform design with distinct global and local certificates.
statements.gap: Bodik--Chavez-Demoulin supplies neither a finite PGF grid nor quantitative global-injectivity and Jacobian margins over compact boxes.
statements.consumer: It supplies the consistency check that the reusable certificate is searching for a nonvacuous finite-input object.

statements.statement: For \(p\geq3\), fixed \(\iota\), and finite \(\Xi\), the procedure terminates after at most \(G_{\#}2^{c_{\max}}+G_{\#}2^{b_{\max}}+(G_{\#}+\binom{G_{\#}}{2})4^{b_{\max}}\) chart or objective leaves and \(\mathfrak B(\Xi)\) outward-rounded operations. It rejects \(\rho\notin\Delta_J^{\mathbb Q}\) before covariance or required-well evaluation. A \(\mathtt{CERTIFIED}\) output proves full rank; normalized allocation with \(\rho_j>0\) for every composition row entering the unpooling map; valid chart coverage; positive exact untruncated bounds \(\Gamma_{\mathcal T}\geq\underline\Gamma_{\mathcal T}\), \(\kappa_{\mathcal T}\geq\underline\kappa_{\mathcal T}\), \(\Lambda_{\mathcal T}(r_{\mathrm{id}})\geq\underline\Lambda_{\mathcal T}(r_{\mathrm{id}})\), and \(\mu_{\mathcal T}(r_{\mathrm{id}};\mathscr C)\geq\underline\mu_{\mathcal T}(r_{\mathrm{id}};\mathscr C)\); positive interiority; the recorded tail and variance bounds; and \(N_{\mathrm{req}}\leq N_{\max}\). For an empty wrong-graph comparison or remote-pair set, the corresponding exact and certified bounds are \(+\infty\) and impose no numerical check. A \(\mathtt{REFUTED}\) output proves its named obstruction; \(\mathtt{UNDECIDED}\) makes no substantive claim. If all nonvacuous exact inequalities have strict slack and the deterministic chart construction admits strict strong-monotonicity bounds, sufficiently large finite truncation, subdivision, Taylor, and precision controls produce \(\mathtt{CERTIFIED}\).
statements.justification: This is the proof-producing kernel with distinct global identification, local regularity, and precision outputs.
statements.gap: Rump, Kearfott, and Berz--Makino do not jointly propagate Poisson-PGF tails through graph exclusion, global within-graph identification, singular values, covariance, and intervention precision.
statements.consumer: It turns a prospective choice of composition, grid, model boxes, and computational budget into an auditable go, stop, or undecided decision.

statements.statement: Assume \(p\geq3\), fix \(\iota\), and let \(\mathfrak C(\Xi)=\mathtt{CERTIFIED}\). Suppose the true pooled model has \(\boldsymbol D_0\in\mathfrak G\) and \(\theta_0\in\Theta^{\mathrm{in}}_{\boldsymbol D_0}\), the normalized allocation obeys \(\rho\in\Delta_J^{\mathbb Q}\) with \(\rho_j>0\) for every row and \(n_{Sj}/N_S\to\rho_j\) for \(S\in\{A,B\}\), and the weighting and nondegeneracy conditions hold. As \(\min(N_A,N_B)\to\infty\), the declared lexicographic selector satisfies \(\Pr(\widehat{\boldsymbol D}=\boldsymbol D_0)\to1\), while \(\sqrt{N_B}(\widehat{\boldsymbol\tau}-\boldsymbol\tau)\Rightarrow\mathcal N(0,V_\tau(\boldsymbol D_0,\theta_0;\iota))\). Plug-in covariance is consistent and scalar Wald intervals have pointwise coverage \(1-\alpha\). The conclusion separately uses certified wrong-graph separation, certified global within-graph uniqueness, certified local nonsingularity, certified positive inference-box clearance, the normalized row allocation, and the deterministic selector. Moreover \(\lVert\Sigma_g\rVert_2\leq\lVert\operatorname{diag}(g)\rVert_2^2\lVert M^+\rVert_2^2\lVert\operatorname{diag}(h)^{-1}\rVert_2^2\lVert\Sigma_h\rVert_2\).
statements.justification: The inference layer uses exactly the global, local, interior, selector, and covariance objects certified by the decision layer.
statements.gap: Chen--Cao--Bu and Carrasco--Florens provide transform-moment ingredients, but neither conditions graph-selected intervention inference on a matching validated global certificate with propagated precision bounds.
statements.consumer: A certified prospective benchmark obtains uncertainty from replicate wells without manufacturing pseudo-single-cell observations.

statements.justification: This checks the general inverse against the smallest genuinely mixed full-rank design.
statements.gap: The calculation is a sanity reduction and is not presented as a novelty claim.
statements.consumer: It provides an auditable population inverse for the synthetic two-type application.

statements.statement: For \(p\geq3\) and fixed \(\iota\), determine the finite Pareto set \(\mathfrak P_{\mathrm{adm}}\) over \(\mathfrak X_{\mathrm{adm}}\): integer matrices have \(J\leq J_{\max}\) and entries at most \(m_{\max}\); grids are subsets of the fixed finite rational set \(\mathcal Z_{\mathrm{cand}}\) with cardinality at most \(L_{\max}\); normalized nonnegative rational allocations and well caps lie in \(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{adm}}\subset\Delta_J^{\mathbb Q}\) and \(\mathcal N_{\mathrm{adm}}\); and truncation, moment, Taylor, objective-subdivision, chart-subdivision, precision, and arithmetic work obey the fixed policy and \(\mathfrak b\). Can certified dominance and infeasibility rules characterize the finite frontier in graph gap, Jacobian margin, global-identification margins, required wells, contrast half-width, and arithmetic cost without evaluating every admissible input?
statements.justification: The question poses a finite auditable design frontier under declared statistical and computational budgets.
statements.gap: Validated global optimization certifies numerical ranges, and tomography design optimizes information, but no result characterizes a joint certified region for Poisson-PGF graph exclusion, immersion, and causal-contrast precision.
statements.consumer: It yields a reusable finite menu of nondominated prospective designs.

statements.statement: Run \(\mathfrak C\) on the complete rational input \(\Xi_0\) in \(\mathrm{def{:}fixed\text{-}protocol}\). If and only if its status is \(\mathtt{UNDECIDED}\), run it once more on the uniquely prescribed replacement \(\Xi_1=\mathfrak F_0(\Xi_0)\); do not refine after \(\mathtt{CERTIFIED}\) or \(\mathtt{REFUTED}\). Does one of these two runs return \(\mathtt{CERTIFIED}\), thereby proving positive nonvacuous wrong-graph, Jacobian, remote-identification, and local-injectivity bounds, valid tails, and \(N_{\mathrm{req}}\leq200000\) for the synthetic \(p=3\), \((i_X,i_Y,i_Z)=(1,2,3)\) benchmark?
statements.justification: This is a falsifiable application of the reusable procedure, not the headline theorem and not evidence for an existing biological assay.
statements.gap: The floating-point pilot checks only two local witness Jacobians and no wrong-graph boxes; it does not establish any uniform premise used by the inference theorem.
statements.consumer: A certified answer licenses only the stated synthetic prospective benchmark; a collision, singularity, or precision obstruction stops that protocol without affecting the rank frontier.

statements.statement: If \(\mathfrak C(\Xi)\) returns \(\mathtt{CERTIFIED}\), its recorded valid cover \(\mathscr C\) satisfies \(\mu_{\mathcal T}(r_{\mathrm{id}};\mathscr C)\geq\underline\mu_{\mathcal T}>0\), so every same-graph pair closer than \(r_{\mathrm{id}}\) is separated in a co-containing chart. Every feasible pair at least \(r_{\mathrm{id}}\) apart has squared \(W\)-distance at least \(\underline\Lambda_{\mathcal T}>0\), with the remote claim vacuous when that pair set is empty. Therefore every \(m_{\boldsymbol d,\mathcal T}\) is globally injective on \(\Theta_{\boldsymbol d}\), and \(Q_{\boldsymbol d,\mathcal T}(\cdot;m_{\boldsymbol d,\mathcal T}(\theta_0))\) has unique minimum \(\theta_0\) with the certified remote separation outside its local neighborhood.
statements.justification: This prevents local Jacobian rank from substituting for global uniqueness.
statements.gap: A local inverse theorem alone does not certify a unique compact-box population minimum.
statements.consumer: It supplies the global identification premise for the deterministic minimum-distance estimator.

sampling_model.design: Independent replicate wells are collected at fixed, known integer composition rows of \(M\). The two-row matrix \(M_0\) is a synthetic prospective-design application.
sampling_model.units: A unit is one replicate well containing exactly the declared number of independent cells of each labeled type; rowwise random splitting produces \(N_A\) training wells and \(N_B\) inference wells, both split sizes diverge, and the row fractions converge to a normalized rational probability vector \(\rho\) that is strictly positive for every sampled composition row.
sampling_model.treatment: For \(p\geq3\), the ordered embedding \(\iota:\{X,Y,Z\}\hookrightarrow\{1,\ldots,p\}\) is fixed before analysis. The interventions \(\operatorname{do}(V_{i_X}=1)\) and \(\operatorname{do}(V_{i_X}=2)\) are counterfactual count interventions, and responses are the coordinates \(V_{i_Y}\) and \(V_{i_Z}\), evaluated by truncated factorization after type-law and graph recovery.
sampling_model.overlap: Positive Poisson roots and rates give full support on \(\mathbb N_0^p\), so the fixed parent configurations at the designated coordinates \(i_X,i_Y,i_Z\) are observationally supported within the benchmark family.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Pooled PGFs are empirical replicate-well averages; component PGFs use log inversion; graph and parameter estimates use the deterministic lexicographic sample-split selector; the certifier validates allocation normalization before covariance calculations, and inference is activated only by a certificate of positive sampled-row fractions, wrong-graph separation, global within-graph injectivity, local nonsingularity, positive interiority clearance, and precision.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The paper uses cumulant or transform inversion to recover independent additive link-delay components from aggregate path measurements.
Theorems 1--2 identify component distributions up to shifts, and Section 4 estimates transform mixtures by GMM.
Theorem 2 obtains component recovery under pairwise column independence for a generalized-hyperexponential approximation class.
The paper uses causal minimality and pairwise identifiability to recover a CPCM DAG from its direct observational law while permitting arbitrary source-node laws.

Definition 3 specifies PT-SEM from direct observational count vectors; Theorem 12 identifies its DAG, thinning matrix, and node-wise exogenous distributions under (A1)--(A3), and Theorem 18 proves plug-in BIC selection consistency under (A1)--(A5).
Section 4.2 studies functional consistency under linear aggregation and gives affine ANM/PNL consequences; Section 4.3 concerns conditional-independence consistency.
The paper establishes consistency, asymptotic normality, and covariance weighting for finite or continuum moments.
The article develops mathematically rigorous verification methods based on directed floating-point and interval arithmetic.
The article distinguishes rigorous from non-rigorous deterministic branch-and-bound and reviews sound interval relaxations and termination claims.
The paper combines Taylor-model enclosures with branch-and-bound for rigorous global search.
The paper constructs rigorous interval quasiconvex relaxations for self-validating constrained global optimization.
Theorems 2 and 4 certify approximate polynomial roots and common associated roots.
The paper optimizes network-tomography probe allocation using Fisher information.

tldr: Known linearly independent raw-count compositions recover unrestricted labeled type laws for arbitrary \(p\geq1\) by a logarithmic count-PGF inverse that draws on Shih--Hero's independent-additive transform-inversion idea, with positive Poisson aliases proving necessity. For \(p\geq3\), a fixed ordered embedding defines one exposure and two responses. The headline finite-input certifier constructs and verifies a rational chart-projection cover and separately proves wrong-graph separation, global within-graph injectivity, local Jacobian nonsingularity, interiority clearance, PGF-tail control, and designated-contrast precision. Its deterministic selector supports pointwise sample-split Wald inference. The design frontier is finite under explicit caps, and the fully specified three-node input is a synthetic prospective benchmark with exactly one allowed refinement.

project_justification.gap: Transform inversion, direct-law CPCM and Poisson-thinning DAG identification, and validated numerics are established separately, but no result recovers labeled type laws through known multi-composition pools and propagates infinite-support PGF tails through distinct wrong-graph, global within-graph, local-regularity, and causal-precision certificates.
project_justification.niche: Prospective known-composition designs need a proof-producing decision rule whose global identification, local inference, and measurable selection premises are exactly declared.
project_justification.fill: The project combines the arbitrary-dimensional rank frontier with a finite \(p\geq3\) certifier that constructs and verifies a rational chart-projection cover, a deterministic estimator, an arithmetic ceiling, and a finite Pareto design class.

related_work: Shih--Hero is credited at the source-verified level for transform inversion of independent additive link delays; no unavailable primary-source equation or rank premise is attributed to it. The displayed count-PGF inverse and the positive unrestricted converse are derived in the rank theorem. Chen--Cao--Bu and Thoppe inform transform estimation and restricted tomography identification. Bodik--Chavez-Demoulin, Definition 10 and Lemma 11, supplies pairwise identifiability and recovery of a causally minimal CPCM DAG from its direct law. Its CPCM framework permits arbitrary source-node laws; Poisson roots and positive-polynomial non-root kernels are stricter conditions maintained by this paper. Gao--Cai--Hara, Definition 3, Proposition 10, Theorem 12, and Theorem 18, identifies a Poisson-thinning DAG, thinning coefficients, and exogenous laws from the direct observational count law and gives consistent plug-in BIC selection; its input is not a collection of known multi-composition pools, and it supplies neither labeled type-law unpooling nor a joint PGF-tail, graph-gap, global-injectivity, and causal-precision certificate. Luo--Sun--Zhang Section 4.2 studies functional consistency under linear aggregation and gives affine ANM/PNL consequences; Section 4.3 concerns conditional-independence consistency. Known labeled multi-composition pools remain outside its target. These results motivate prospective auxiliary composition information rather than a claim that all recoverability is restricted to linear aggregation or a claim about normalized legacy bulk data. Carrasco--Florens and Newey--McFadden inform minimum distance, global extremum identification, measurable selection, and delta inference. Rump, Sections 2--4 and 10, supplies directed rounding and verified linear algebra; Kearfott supplies rigorous global-optimization semantics; Berz--Makino and Jansson supply validated Taylor and interval relaxations. Hauenstein--Sottile informs local root checks but not compact analytic image exclusion. The new ingredient is joint propagation of analytic Poisson-PGF tails through wrong-graph exclusion, a verified chart-projection cover, remote within-graph separation, local singular values, pooled covariance, and designated causal precision.
technical_internal_limitation: The \(27\)-point floating-point pilot is not a certificate. Its two local Jacobian singular values are approximately \(0.00326480\) and \(0.00262027\), but it checks neither global within-graph uniqueness nor every wrong-graph box, tail error, or rigorous precision. The reusable procedure may return \(\mathtt{UNDECIDED}\) or certify an obstruction.
honest_scope: Unrestricted rank recovery and stability apply for arbitrary \(p\geq1\). Causal transfer, certification, benchmark contrasts, precision, and Wald inference require \(p\geq3\) and the same explicit ordered embedding \(\iota\); covariance and Wald claims additionally use a normalized allocation with strictly positive fractions for every sampled composition row. Global injectivity is certified by local chart monotonicity plus remote pair separation, never inferred from a positive Jacobian singular value; singleton candidate classes and empty remote-pair sets use the explicit \(+\infty\) convention. The synthetic coefficient box has no assay calibration, and the benchmark has only the displayed base input and one displayed refinement. No claim covers unknown thinning, normalization, composition error, shared well noise, hidden types, high-dimensional growth, or uniform post-selection coverage. Under \(M=M_0\), \(G_1=H_1^2/H_2\) and \(G_2=H_2/H_1\).

seed_details.anchor_location: Acta Numerica, pages 287--449, especially Sections 2--4 and 10; paired with Kearfott (2011), pages 259--279, and Berz--Makino (2009), Sections 1--3
seed_details.kernel: For \(p\geq3\) and a fixed ordered embedding \(\iota\) of one exposure and two response coordinates, construct a reusable finite-input tri-valued certifier that builds a rational chart-projection cover and jointly encloses Poisson-PGF tails, wrong-graph distances, global within-graph identification, all within-graph Jacobians, and propagated \(\iota\)-indexed intervention-contrast variances, with sound termination and an explicit arithmetic ceiling.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Construct inflated rational chart cells by a deterministic finite subdivision, certify projected strong monotonicity on each cell, and combine it with remote same-graph pair separation instead of inferring uniqueness from Jacobian rank.
seed_details.destination_search: Validated numerics covers directed rounding, interval global optimization, and Taylor models separately; no located result specializes them to infinite-support Poisson causal PGFs with a joint statistical precision output.
seed_details.red_team_objection: This is only an application of interval branch-and-bound.
